q: A train travels uniformly at $90\,\text{km/h}$. How far does it travel in $20\,\text{min}$?
a: The time in hours is $t = 20\,\text{min} = \tfrac{1}{3}\,\text{h}$, so $s = vt = 90\,\tfrac{\text{km}}{\text{h}} \cdot \tfrac{1}{3}\,\text{h} = 30\,\text{km}$. The units fit together when the time is in hours.

q: A trolley starts at $4\,\text{m}$ and moves at $3\,\text{m/s}$. At $1\,\text{s}$ it is at $7\,\text{m}$. Is it at $14\,\text{m}$ at $2\,\text{s}$? Justify.
a: No. The position is $s = s_0 + vt = 4\,\text{m} + 3\,\text{m/s} \cdot 2\,\text{s} = 10\,\text{m}$. Only the distance travelled doubles ($3\,\text{m} \to 6\,\text{m}$), because the starting position is not zero.
